analysis:
Integration of all 14 units: docs, changelog fragments, three CLI diagnostic call sites and two test files. Production code is limited to DoctorRunner.swift (lines 34-35, 75-76), DoctorCommand.swift (358-362, 414-415), StatusCommand.swift (135-140) and UnenrollCommand+KeepServing.swift (23-27). The change splits the old strict check into a display decision (`displayedProviderAuthorization`), which keeps an unexpired App Attest lease visible when the last renewal is older than 10s, and a strict removal decision (`currentProviderAuthorization`).

Checks against the threat model:
- The removal gate is unchanged. `unenroll` still reads the strict `currentProviderAuthorization` and gates on `removalReady`, re-checking before and after profile inspection. It now passes `removalAuthorization: authorization`, so its error text stays strict. This preserves T-053 and T-057: stale or late authorization cannot enable premature MDM removal.
- Status and doctor use the displayed lease only to print and to set the pass/warn level. `summary` takes `removalAuthorization` separately, and per the docs and the unit-10 and unit-13 test analyses it gives positive removal advice only when the strict decision matches and `mdm_removal_ready` is set. A late lease shows 'needs fresh coordinator readiness; keep profiles'.
- Coordinator dispatch authorization (TB-002, A-016) is platform-owned and unaffected. The CLI output is not a serving credential, which fits the TB-011 rule that badges and diagnostics grant no permission and the T-052 and T-056 non-overclaim posture.
- No new network calls, key handling, token handling or identifiers are printed. `machineID` printing at StatusCommand.swift:142 is unchanged.

Residual unverified contracts: `ProviderAuthorizationReadiness.swift` and `DaemonStateFile.displayedProviderAuthorization` were not in the replayed source. I could not directly confirm that the display path still enforces process, coordinator, online, protocol and writtenAt checks and the finite `expiresAt > now` check, or that `summary` compares session, machine and reason between the two decisions. The unit-10 pass reviewed the source and the new tests cover these cases. The worst consequence is a diagnostic showing a revoked lease as authorized until `expires_at`, which the docs state openly. This is not a demonstrated regression, and no threat-model update is needed.
